newsitem.title: USA: Freeport-McMoRan to fund MOXY drilling.
newsitem.headline: Freeport-McMoRan to fund MOXY drilling.

text.p: Freeport-McMoRan Resource Partners LP said Tuesday it entered into a $200 million exploration program with McMoRan Oil & Gas Co.

Freeport said it will fund 60 percent of the multi-year program to explore and develop prospects operated by MOXY, offshore in the Gulf of Mexico and onshore in the Gulf Coast area; and all revenues and other costs will be shared equally.

In addition to the MOXY/FRP Exploration Program, Freeport said, it has agreed to purchase MCN Energy Group Inc's MCN's 60 percent interest in the MOXY/MCN offshore exploration program for $43.5 million, subject to adjustments.
To provide capital for these transactions, MOXY intends to undertake a rights offering that could result in Freeport owning a majority of Moxy's stock, the partnership said.
It noted the MOXY/MCN program includes two producing oil and gas fields, eight exploration prospects in the Gulf of Mexico and MOXY's program debt of about $12.5 million.

Subject to completion of the MOXY recapitalization, Freeport said, McMoRan Oil has agreed to acquire Freeport's interest in the MOXY/MCN program's producing properties at the Vermilion Block 160 and 410 fields for $26.0 million and repay Freeport for MOXY's program debt under the MOXY/MCN program.

MOXY and Freeport will contribute their interest in the MOXY/MCN program exploration properties and their interests in seven offshore leases acquired earlier this year to the MOXY/FRP Exploration Program, Freeport said.
It said MOXY anticipates issuing some 28.6 million shares of common stock for an aggregate of about $100 million.

MOXY holders will receive 2.0 transferable subscription rights for each MOXY share held. Each right will entitle the holder to purchase one new MOXY share for $3.50. In addition, each MOXY holder who exercises all rights may also subscribe for shares available as a result of unexercised rights.
In connection with the rights offering, Freeport said, it has set a standby purchase agreement to purchase all shares offered but not purchased at the subscription price.

Upon closing of the rights offering, MOXY will pay Freeport a fee of $6 million representing negotiated compensation for the standby commitment, its agreement to purchase the MCN producing properties for resale to MOXY and its agreement to enter into the MOXY/FRP Exploration Program.
If Freeport does not acquire at least 30 percent of MOXY's common stock the standby commitment, it will have the option to buy enoungh stock at $3.50 per share go gain that interest.

Depending on the number of shares purchased pursuant to the exercise of rights, Freeport pointed out, it may obtain ownership of a majority of MOXY's outstanding common, in which case it would be in a position to control the election of MOXY's directors.
The rights offering and standby purchase agreement are subject to approval by MOXY's stockholders.

If the rights offering and standby agreement are not approved, the rights offering will not occur, the MOXY/FRP Exploration Program will not be established and MOXY will not acquire Freeport's interest in the MOXY/MCN program which would then be expected to terminate except as to commitments previously made.

Freeport said its participation with MOXY in the potentially highly rewarding oil and gas exploration activities in the Gulf Coast area offers the partnership a hedge against price increases for the significant amount of natural gas it consumes in its fertilizer production operations.
